items.text:
गुरुर् अग्निर् द्विजातीनां वर्णानां ब्राह्मणो गुरुः ।
पतिर् एव गुरुः स्त्रीणां सर्वस्याभ्यागतो गुरुः ॥१॥
items.tr:
gurur agnir dvijātīnāṃ varṇānāṃ brāhmaṇo guruḥ |
patir eva guruḥ strīṇāṃ sarvasyābhyāgato guruḥ ||1||
items.en: Fire is the teacher of the twice-born, the Brahmin is the teacher of all classes, the husband is the teacher of the wife, and a guest is to be honoured by everyone.

items.text:
यथा चतुर्भिः कनकं परीक्ष्यते
निघर्षणच्छेदनतापताडनैः ।
तथा चतुर्भिः पुरुषः परीक्ष्यते
त्यागेन शीलेन गुणेन कर्मणा ॥२॥
items.tr:
yathā caturbhiḥ kanakaṃ parīkṣyate
nigharṣaṇacchedanatāpatāḍanaiḥ |
tathā caturbhiḥ puruṣaḥ parīkṣyate
tyāgena śīlena guṇena karmaṇā ||2||
items.en: Just as gold is tested in four ways, by rubbing, cutting, heating and beating, so a person is tested in four ways: by giving, by character, by qualities and by deeds.

items.text:
तावद्भयेन भेतव्यं यावद् भयमनागतम् ।
आगतं तु भयं वीक्ष्यं प्रहर्तव्यमशंकया ॥३॥
items.tr:
tāvadbhayena bhetavyaṃ yāvad bhayamanāgatam |
āgataṃ tu bhayaṃ vīkṣyaṃ prahartavyamaśaṃkayā ||3||
items.en: Fear danger only while it has not yet come; once it has come, face it and strike without hesitation.

items.text:
एकोदरसमुद्भूता एकनक्षत्रजातकाः ।
न भवन्ति समाः शीला यथा बदरिकण्टकाः ॥४॥
items.tr:
ekodarasamudbhūtā ekanakṣatrajātakāḥ |
na bhavanti samāḥ śīlā yathā badarikaṇṭakāḥ ||4||
items.en: Children born from the same womb and under the same star are still not alike in nature, just as the thorns of the jujube bush are all different.

items.text:
निःस्पृहो नाधिकारी स्यान्नाकामो मण्डनप्रियः ।
नाऽविदग्धः प्रियंब्रूयात् स्पष्टवक्ता न वञ्चकः ॥५॥
items.tr:
niḥspṛho nādhikārī syānnākāmo maṇḍanapriyaḥ |
nā'vidagdhaḥ priyaṃbrūyāt spaṣṭavaktā na vañcakaḥ ||5||
items.en: One with no desire will not seek office, one with no lust will not care for adornment, one without skill cannot speak pleasingly, and one who speaks plainly is no cheat.

items.text:
मूर्खाणां पण्डिता द्वेष्या अधनानां महाधनाः ।
वरांगना कुलस्त्रीणां सुभगानां च दुर्भगा ॥६॥
items.tr:
mūrkhāṇāṃ paṇḍitā dveṣyā adhanānāṃ mahādhanāḥ |
varāṃganā kulastrīṇāṃ subhagānāṃ ca durbhagā ||6||
items.en: Fools hate the learned, the poor hate the rich, women of good family hate courtesans, and unlucky women resent the lucky.

items.text:
आलस्योपगता विद्या परहस्तगतं धनम् ।
अल्पबीजं हतं क्षेत्रं हतं सैन्यमनायकम् ॥७॥
items.tr:
ālasyopagatā vidyā parahastagataṃ dhanam |
alpabījaṃ hataṃ kṣetraṃ hataṃ sainyamanāyakam ||7||
items.en: Learning is lost through laziness, money is lost when it is in another's hands, a field sown with too little seed is lost, and an army without a leader is lost.

items.text:
अभ्यासाध्दार्यते विद्या कुलं शीलेन धार्यते ।
गुणेन ज्ञायते त्वार्यः कोपो नेत्रेण गम्यते ॥८॥
items.tr:
abhyāsādhdāryate vidyā kulaṃ śīlena dhāryate |
guṇena jñāyate tvāryaḥ kopo netreṇa gamyate ||8||
items.en: Learning is kept by practice, a family is kept by good conduct, a noble person is known by his qualities, and anger is seen in the eyes.

items.text:
वित्तेन रक्ष्यते धर्मो विद्या योगेन रक्ष्यते ।
मृदुना रक्ष्यते भूपः सत्स्त्रिया रक्ष्यते गृहम् ॥९॥
items.tr:
vittena rakṣyate dharmo vidyā yogena rakṣyate |
mṛdunā rakṣyate bhūpaḥ satstriyā rakṣyate gṛham ||9||
items.en: Religion is protected by wealth, learning by practice, a king by gentleness, and a home by a good wife.

items.text:
अन्यथा वेदपाण्डित्यं शास्त्रमाचारमन्यथा ।
अन्यथा वदता शांतंलोकाःक्लिश्यन्ति चाऽन्यथा ॥१०॥
items.tr:
anyathā vedapāṇḍityaṃ śāstramācāramanyathā |
anyathā vadatā śāṃtaṃlokāḥkliśyanti cā'nyathā ||10||
items.en: Those who speak ill of the learning of the Vedas, of the scriptures, of good conduct and of peaceful people only bring suffering on themselves for nothing.

items.text:
दारिद्र्यनाशनं दान शीलं दुर्गतिनाशनम् ।
अज्ञाननाशिनी प्रज्ञा भावना भयनाशिनी ॥११॥
items.tr:
dāridryanāśanaṃ dāna śīlaṃ durgatināśanam |
ajñānanāśinī prajñā bhāvanā bhayanāśinī ||11||
items.en: Giving removes poverty, good conduct removes misfortune, wisdom removes ignorance, and devotion removes fear.

items.text:
नास्ति कामसमो व्याधिर्नास्ति मोहसमो रिपुः ।
नास्ति कोपसमो वह्नि र्नास्ति ज्ञानात्परं सुखम् ॥१२॥
items.tr:
nāsti kāmasamo vyādhirnāsti mohasamo ripuḥ |
nāsti kopasamo vahni rnāsti jñānātparaṃ sukham ||12||
items.en: There is no disease like desire, no enemy like delusion, no fire like anger, and no happiness greater than knowledge.

items.text:
जन्ममृत्युं हि यात्येको भुनक्त्येकं शुभाशुभम् ।
नरकेषु पतत्येक एको याति परां गतिम् ॥१३॥
items.tr:
janmamṛtyuṃ hi yātyeko bhunaktyekaṃ śubhāśubham |
narakeṣu patatyeka eko yāti parāṃ gatim ||13||
items.en: A person is born alone and dies alone; alone he reaps the good and bad of his deeds; alone he falls into hell, and alone he reaches the highest state.

items.text:
तृणं ब्रह्मविदः स्वर्गस्तृणं शूरस्य जीवितम् ।
जिताक्षस्य तृणं नारी निःस्पृहस्य तृणं जगत् ॥१४॥
items.tr:
tṛṇaṃ brahmavidaḥ svargastṛṇaṃ śūrasya jīvitam |
jitākṣasya tṛṇaṃ nārī niḥspṛhasya tṛṇaṃ jagat ||14||
items.en: To one who knows God, heaven is worth no more than straw; to the brave, life is straw; to one who has mastered his senses, a woman is straw; to one free of desire, the whole world is straw.

items.text:
विद्या मित्रं प्रवासेषु भार्या मित्रं गृहेषु च ।
व्यधितस्यौषधं मित्रं धर्मो मित्रं मृतस्य च ॥१५॥
items.tr:
vidyā mitraṃ pravāseṣu bhāryā mitraṃ gṛheṣu ca |
vyadhitasyauṣadhaṃ mitraṃ dharmo mitraṃ mṛtasya ca ||15||
items.en: Learning is a friend when you travel, a wife is a friend at home, medicine is a friend to the sick, and good deeds are a friend after death.

items.text:
वृथा वृष्टिस्समुद्रेषु वृथा तृप्तेषु भोजनम् ।
वृथा दानं धनाढ्येषु वृथा दीपोऽदीवाऽपि च ॥१६॥
items.tr:
vṛthā vṛṣṭissamudreṣu vṛthā tṛpteṣu bhojanam |
vṛthā dānaṃ dhanāḍhyeṣu vṛthā dīpo'dīvā'pi ca ||16||
items.en: Rain on the ocean is wasted, food given to one who is full is wasted, gifts to the rich are wasted, and a lamp in daylight is wasted.

items.text:
नास्ति मेघसमं तोयं नास्ति चात्मसमं बलम् ।
नास्तिचक्षुः समं तेजो नास्ति धान्यसमं प्रियम् ॥१७॥
items.tr:
nāsti meghasamaṃ toyaṃ nāsti cātmasamaṃ balam |
nāsticakṣuḥ samaṃ tejo nāsti dhānyasamaṃ priyam ||17||
items.en: There is no water like rain water, no strength like your own, no light like the eyes, and nothing dearer than grain.

items.text:
अधना धनमिच्छन्ति वाचं चैव चतुष्पदः ।
मानवाः स्वर्गमिच्छन्ति मोक्षमिच्छन्तिदेवताः ॥१८॥
items.tr:
adhanā dhanamicchanti vācaṃ caiva catuṣpadaḥ |
mānavāḥ svargamicchanti mokṣamicchantidevatāḥ ||18||
items.en: The poor want wealth, animals want speech, humans want heaven, and the gods want freedom from rebirth.

items.text:
स्त्येन धार्यते पृथ्वी स्त्येन तपते रविः ।
स्त्येन वाति वायुश्च सर्वं सत्ये प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥१९॥
items.tr:
styena dhāryate pṛthvī styena tapate raviḥ |
styena vāti vāyuśca sarvaṃ satye pratiṣṭhitam ||19||
items.en: Truth holds up the earth, truth makes the sun shine, truth makes the wind blow; everything rests on truth.

items.text:
चला लक्ष्मीश्चलाः प्राणश्चले जीवितमन्दिरे ।
चलाऽचले च संसारे धर्म एको हि निश्चलः ॥२०॥
items.tr:
calā lakṣmīścalāḥ prāṇaścale jīvitamandire |
calā'cale ca saṃsāre dharma eko hi niścalaḥ ||20||
items.en: Wealth is unsteady, breath is unsteady, life and home are unsteady; in this moving and unmoving world, only righteousness stays firm.

items.text:
नराणां नापितो धूर्तः पक्षिणां चैव वायसः ।
चतुष्पदां श्रृगालस्तु स्त्रीणां धुर्ता च मालिनी ॥२१॥
items.tr:
narāṇāṃ nāpito dhūrtaḥ pakṣiṇāṃ caiva vāyasaḥ |
catuṣpadāṃ śrṛgālastu strīṇāṃ dhurtā ca mālinī ||21||
items.en: Among men the barber is the cunning one, among birds the crow, among beasts the jackal, and among women the flower-seller.

items.text:
जनिता चोपनेता च यस्तु विद्यां प्रयच्छति ।
अन्नदाता भयत्राता पञ्चैते पितरः स्मृताः ॥२२॥
items.tr:
janitā copanetā ca yastu vidyāṃ prayacchati |
annadātā bhayatrātā pañcaite pitaraḥ smṛtāḥ ||22||
items.en: These five are counted as fathers: the one who gives birth, the one who performs the sacred-thread ceremony, the one who teaches, the one who gives food, and the one who protects from fear.

items.text:
राजपत्नी गुरोः पत्नी मित्र पत्नी तथैव च ।
पत्नी माता स्वमाता च पञ्चैता मातरः स्मृता ॥२३॥
items.tr:
rājapatnī guroḥ patnī mitra patnī tathaiva ca |
patnī mātā svamātā ca pañcaitā mātaraḥ smṛtā ||23||
items.en: These five are counted as mothers: the king's wife, the teacher's wife, a friend's wife, one's wife's mother, and one's own mother.
